preamble: Lenition of postvocalic /d/ to the palatal glide [j], probably through a fricative stage [ð]. Between Old and Middle Persian, postvocalic *d became y, as in Old Persian pād(a) 'foot' > Middle and New Persian pāy and Proto-Iranian *madu > Middle Persian may 'wine'. In Turkic, Proto-Turkic *d (often written *δ) became y in the Oghuz and Kipchak languages, giving Turkish ayak 'foot' and kuyruk 'tail' beside Old Turkic adaq, qudruq; other branches show d, t or z instead, which is the basis of the classic d/t/z/y classification of Turkic. Cases in Romance such as Latin hodie > Spanish hoy involve coalescence of the cluster /dj/ with the yod and belong elsewhere.

examples.note: The same postvocalic *d > y, word-finally after loss of the final vowel.
Compare Tuvan adak, Yakut ataq and Khakas azax, which keep or change the dental differently.
Compare Tuvan kuduruk, Yakut kuturuk, Khakas xuzurux.
Kipchak shares the y-reflex with Oghuz.
Before a consonant the glide forms a diphthong with the preceding vowel.
